papers.title: Plasma proteomic profiles associated with low-dose computed tomography findings and incident lung cancer: a prospective pilot study.
papers.abstract: Plasma proteins may reflect tumor-host biology, but their relationships with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) findings and incident lung cancer remain uncertain. Although LDCT screening has improved survival, challenges remain in risk stratification and interpretation of screening findings. The aim of the present study was to investigate associations between plasma proteomic profiles, LDCT findings and incident lung cancer, and to explore their potential for lung cancer risk stratification.
papers.summary: This prospective pilot study examined whether plasma protein profiles are associated with low-dose CT (LDCT) screening findings and the subsequent development of lung cancer. The authors aimed to see if proteomic data could improve risk stratification and help interpret screening results beyond imaging alone. As a pilot, it primarily explores feasibility and preliminary associations rather than establishing validated biomarkers.

papers.title: Identification of hepatitis B virus-associated membrane proteins as prognostic biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma based on retrospective analysis of integrated membrane proteomics.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is one of the major risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development. Current prognostic assessment of HBV-associated HCC (HBV-HCC) largely relies on clinicopathological parameters, such as tumor stage, liver function, and serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels, which have limited accuracy in identifying patients at high risk of recurrence or poor survival. Therefore, reliable molecular biomarkers are urgently needed to improve individualized risk stratification and guide postoperative surveillance and therapeutic decision-making. HBV infection induce
papers.summary: This study used integrated membrane proteomics on retrospective patient samples to identify hepatitis B virus-associated membrane proteins that could serve as prognostic biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma. The goal is to improve risk stratification beyond current clinicopathological parameters like tumor stage and AFP levels, which have limited accuracy for predicting recurrence or survival.

papers.title: Analysis and validation of prognostic markers for thyroid cancer by single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Thyroid cancer represents the most prevalent malignancy within the endocrine system, exhibiting consistent increasing incidence rates over the years. We aim to utilize single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset to analyze key genes associated with prognosis in thyroid cancer.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing combined with bulk RNA sequencing to identify genes associated with prognosis in thyroid cancer. The authors analyze scRNA-seq data to pinpoint key prognostic markers and then validate them in bulk transcriptomic cohorts, aiming to improve risk stratification for this increasingly common endocrine malignancy.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomics and Machine Learning Nominate IL15- and PPP2R1A-Centered Programs in PTSD Using Pathway-Informed Autonomic-Cardiac Gene Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with immune and autonomic disturbances, but molecular programs linking PTSD-related blood transcriptional signals with autonomic-cardiac biology remain incompletely characterized. The public Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) cohorts analyzed here did not directly measure palpitations or autonomic dysfunction. Peripheral-blood transcriptomes from GSE81761 and GSE63878 were integrated with a prespecified pathway-derived autonomic-cardiac gene set constructed from Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways. Genes overlapping the curated
papers.summary: This study integrated two public peripheral-blood transcriptome datasets from PTSD patients with a curated autonomic-cardiac gene set derived from KEGG pathways, then applied machine learning to prioritize candidate genes. The analysis nominated IL15- and PPP2R1A-centered molecular programs as potential links between PTSD-related immune signaling and autonomic-cardiac dysfunction, though the cohorts did not directly measure palpitations or autonomic symptoms.

papers.title: AIS-Informed and Land-Aware Eco-Routing for Maritime Decision Support Using Machine Learning and Metocean Data.
papers.abstract: Geospatial sensing and data analytics can support maritime risk and safety management by transforming vessel-movement and environmental observations into transparent evidence for route assessment. Within this context, reducing maritime fuel consumption requires routing methods that exploit historical vessel-movement data while representing geographical and metocean conditions explicitly. This study contributes an AIS-informed, land-aware eco-routing framework that integrates geospatial data processing, machine-learning-based fuel estimation, and weather-screening analysis to generate minimum-p
papers.summary: This study develops an eco-routing framework for maritime vessels that combines AIS tracking data, machine-learning-based fuel consumption estimation, and metocean (weather and ocean) data to generate fuel-minimizing routes. The approach explicitly accounts for land boundaries and screens weather conditions, providing transparent evidence to support maritime decision-making. The work demonstrates how geospatial sensing and data analytics can be integrated to reduce fuel use and improve maritime risk management.

papers.title: ATPPred: Prediction of Plant ATP-Binding Proteins Using ESM2 and 1D Convolution.
papers.abstract: Plant ATP-binding proteins play a central role in various physiological processes in plants, including growth and development, energy metabolism, signal transduction, and environmental adaptation. Accurately identifying ATP-binding proteins from plant protein sequences is crucial for a deeper understanding of plant physiology and their applications in agricultural biotechnology. In this study, we propose ATPPred, a tool based on the protein large language model Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2 (ESM2) and a 1-dimensional convolutional neural network for the high-precision prediction of plant ATP-b
papers.summary: ATPPred is a computational tool that predicts whether a plant protein binds ATP, using the protein language model ESM2 to generate sequence embeddings and a 1D convolutional neural network for classification. The authors report high-accuracy performance, offering a practical resource for annotating plant proteomes and supporting plant physiology and agricultural biotechnology research.

papers.title: Needle-Free Bedside and Anthropometric Measures Show Weak Discrimination of an Adverse Blood-Biomarker Profile in Middle-Aged and Older Mexican Adults: An Internally Validated Machine-Learning Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Needle-free measures such as grip strength, gait speed, and anthropometry are attractive as potential substitutes for blood-based biomarkers in low-resource settings, yet whether they can predict an adverse blood-biomarker profile remains unknown. This study aimed to determine whether machine-learning algorithms can predict such a profile from a defined set of needle-free bedside and anthropometric measures in Mexican adults. Methods: Using the Mexican Health and Aging Study (MHAS) 2012 biomarker subsample (n = 2000; mean age 62.4 years; 59.8% women), we defined a blood-
papers.summary: Using data from 2,000 middle-aged and older Mexican adults, the authors tested whether simple needle-free measures (grip strength, gait speed, anthropometry) could predict an adverse blood-biomarker profile via machine learning. Despite internal validation, discrimination was weak, suggesting these bedside measures are poor substitutes for blood-based biomarkers in this population.

papers.title: A Drug-Referenced Machine-Learning Framework for Prioritizing Korean Herbal Formulations in Hypertension Using Linear SVM and Graph Convolutional Networks.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is regulated by interacting molecular systems, providing a rationale for network-based screening of multicomponent therapeutic candidates. Grounded in the conceptual framework of network pharmacology, we developed a hypertension-focused computational framework to prioritize insurance-covered Korean herbal formulations using protein-protein interaction networks derived from marketed antihypertensive and comparator drugs. Thirty reference-drug graphs (15 antihypertensive and 15 comparator drugs) were evaluated using four molecular classifiers under repeated group-aware nested cross-
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline that uses protein-protein interaction networks seeded by known antihypertensive drugs to rank Korean herbal formulations for hypertension. They compared four classifiers, including linear SVM and graph convolutional networks, using repeated group-aware nested cross-validation across 30 reference-drug graphs. The framework is intended to help prioritize insurance-covered herbal candidates for further study.

papers.title: Machine learning uncovers previously undetectable genetic deletions in cancer panel sequencing.
papers.abstract: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions mi
papers.summary: The authors developed a machine-learning pipeline to detect focal genetic deletions that standard copy-number pipelines like TSO500 miss in cancer panel sequencing. Focusing on PTEN loss (which can guide mTOR/Akt inhibitor therapy), an XGBoost model trained on deleted versus wild-type tumors identified previously undetectable focal deletions and evaluated zygosity. This could help more patients qualify for targeted therapy.

papers.title: Cross-domain signal grammars of transcription termination.
papers.abstract: Transcription termination establishes gene boundaries, recycles RNA polymerase, and prevents interference between neighboring transcription units. Termination depends on cis-acting elements, trans-acting factors, and the susceptibility of the elongation complex to pausing, cleavage, destabilization, or release. Predicted motifs, stable RNA ends, processing sites, readthrough regions, and polymerase-release regions are nevertheless often treated as measurements of the same event, which complicates mechanistic comparison and model development. This review compares termination signals as context-
papers.summary: This review argues that diverse transcription termination signals—predicted motifs, stable RNA ends, processing sites, readthrough regions, and polymerase-release regions—are often conflated as measurements of the same event, which hinders mechanistic comparison and model development. It proposes comparing termination signals as context-dependent 'grammars' across domains, integrating cis-elements, trans-factors, and elongation-complex susceptibility to define termination outcomes.

papers.title: AI Model Reporting Standards in Health Care: Systematic Review and Consolidation.
papers.abstract: AI technologies are currently experiencing significant growth in development and use in health care. The AI model lifecycle includes several stages, all of which should be adequately described. Reporting standards are commonly used for this purpose. However, the plain-text structure of these standards prevents transparent machine-readability of this information.
papers.summary: This systematic review consolidates existing reporting standards for AI models in health care, highlighting that current standards are plain-text and not machine-readable. The authors argue for restructuring these standards to enable transparent, automated assessment of AI model reporting throughout its lifecycle.

papers.title: Protein Language Models Identify Early Folding Residues as Critical Hotspots for Pathogenic Variants and Cancer Prognosis.
papers.abstract: Identifying the specific residues that initiate protein folding is critical for understanding protein stability and the mechanisms of misfolding-related diseases. However, the systematic, proteome-wide identification of these early folding residues (EFRs) has been hampered by both experimental and computational limitations. Here, we present LMEFold, a deep learning framework using protein language models (PLMs) to accurately predict EFRs from amino acid sequence alone. LMEFold outperforms existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831), and its predicted scores
papers.summary: LMEFold is a deep learning framework that uses protein language models to predict early folding residues (EFRs) directly from amino acid sequence, outperforming existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831). The authors show that these predicted EFRs are enriched for pathogenic variants and are associated with cancer prognosis, suggesting folding-initiation sites are functional hotspots.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the landscape of machine learning applications in dementia research, covering diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. It surveys trends, prediction goals, data modalities, and collaborative networks to highlight emerging computational approaches in the field.

papers.title: Identification of Mitochondrial Dynamics-Related Genes as Diagnostic Biomarkers for Osteoarthritis Using Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, painful joint disease whose early diagnosis is critical for effective treatment. Since mitochondrial dynamics have been implicated in the onset and progression of OA, this study aimed to explore the diagnostic value of mitochondrial dynamics-related genes (MDRGs) in OA.
papers.summary: This study applies weighted gene co-expression network analysis and machine learning to identify mitochondrial dynamics-related genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers for osteoarthritis. The work aims to support earlier detection of OA, which is critical for effective treatment, by linking mitochondrial dynamics to disease onset and progression.

papers.title: CatRange enables robust prediction of enzyme variant kinetic regimes.
papers.abstract: Predicting enzyme kinetics directly from sequence remains a central challenge in computational biology, particularly for mutations at catalytically essential residues. Existing models often default to wild-type predictions even when mutations cause substantial activity loss. This limits their utility for enzyme design and mechanistic inference. Here, we introduce CatRange, a machine learning framework trained on CatLog-27k, a human-in-the-loop, AI-agent curated dataset of 27,176 in vitro enzyme-substrate kinetic records. CatLog-27k was created through systematic audit and correction of BRENDA
papers.summary: CatRange is a machine learning framework that predicts enzyme kinetic parameters directly from sequence, including for mutations at catalytically essential residues where existing models often default to wild-type predictions. It was trained on CatLog-27k, a human-in-the-loop, AI-agent curated dataset of 27,176 in vitro enzyme-substrate kinetic records created by auditing and correcting BRENDA. This enables more robust prediction of enzyme variant kinetic regimes for design and mechanistic inference.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Identification of Madecassoside as a Potential RAD51 Modulator That Sensitizes Breast Cancer Cells to Cisplatin.
papers.abstract: Homologous recombination (HR) is an essential pathway for preserving the genomic stability of cells by repairing DNA damage, especially double-strand breaks and interstrand crosslinks. RAD51 recombinase plays a central role in the HR pathway, and when DNA damage occurs, RAD51 binds to single-stranded DNA at the cleavage site to form a helical nucleoprotein filament. Therefore, pharmacological inhibition of RAD51 is emerging as an attractive strategy to block the repair mechanisms of cancer cells and maximize the therapeutic efficacy of conventional radiation and chemotherapy. Several RAD51 sma
papers.summary: This study used machine learning to identify madecassoside as a potential RAD51 modulator, a protein central to homologous recombination DNA repair. The compound sensitized breast cancer cells to cisplatin, suggesting RAD51 inhibition could enhance chemotherapy efficacy. The work combines computational screening with experimental validation in cancer cells.

papers.title: Mechanism of luteolin in treating chronic heart failure by regulating HIF-1 signaling pathway-mediated mitochondrial damage to inhibit cardiomyocyte apoptosis.
papers.abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a systemic cardiovascular disease characterized by an extremely poor prognosis. Luteolin demonstrates promising therapeutic potential in the prevention and management of CHF. This study aims to explore the mechanism by which luteolin ameliorates CHF through mitigating mitochondrial damage and inhibiting cardiomyocyte apoptosis, using bioinformatics analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experiments.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how luteolin, a plant-derived flavonoid, protects against chronic heart failure by targeting the HIF-1 signaling pathway. Using bioinformatics plus in vitro and in vivo experiments, the authors show that luteolin reduces mitochondrial damage and cardiomyocyte apoptosis, suggesting HIF-1 pathway modulation as the underlying mechanism. The work supports luteolin as a candidate therapeutic for CHF.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing identifies transient receptor potential channel-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: The precise cause of ulcerative colitis (UC) is still unclear. While transient receptor potential (TRP) ion channels are increasingly linked to UC pathophysiology, the comprehensive roles of TRP channel-related genes are not well understood. This study aimed to systematically identify TRP channel-related biomarkers and develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic targets for UC.
papers.summary: This study combines bulk transcriptome data with single-cell RNA sequencing to systematically identify transient receptor potential (TRP) channel-related genes as candidate biomarkers for ulcerative colitis. The authors propose these genes as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets, though the abstract does not report specific validated findings.

papers.title: Reduced hepatic GLUL expression accompanies altered RIP3/MLKL-pathway protein abundance in early cholestatic liver injury following bile duct ligation.
papers.abstract: Obstructive cholestasis is characterized by disturbances in bile acid homeostasis, amino acid metabolism, inflammatory responses, and hepatocellular injury. Although RIP3/MLKL-pathway proteins have been implicated in cholestatic liver damage, their relationship with metabolic alterations remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify necroptosis-related genes and associated metabolic-pathway alterations in early bile duct ligation (BDL)-induced cholestatic liver injury through integrated bioinformatics analyses and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study integrates bioinformatics analysis with experimental validation to examine early liver injury after bile duct ligation in a rodent model of obstructive cholestasis. The authors report that reduced expression of the metabolic enzyme GLUL (glutamine synthetase) coincides with altered abundance of RIP3/MLKL necroptosis-pathway proteins, suggesting a link between metabolic dysregulation and necroptotic signaling in early cholestatic injury. The work is largely descriptive and based on a single animal model, so the mechanistic relationship between GLUL loss and RIP3/MLKL activation remains to be established.

papers.title: Immune and inflammatory features associated with pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related genes in HFpEF: a machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and myocardial fibrosis. Whether pyroptosis intersects with fibrotic remodeling in HFpEF remains uncertain. Two murine cardiac transcriptomic datasets were integrated after batch correction and intersected with curated pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related gene sets. Functional enrichment, univariate logistic regression, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were us
papers.summary: This study integrates two mouse cardiac transcriptomic datasets to identify genes linking pyroptosis (inflammatory cell death) with myocardial fibrosis in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Using machine learning feature selection (SVM-RFE and LASSO), the authors pinpoint candidate genes and characterize associated immune and inflammatory features. The work suggests that pyroptosis-fibrosis crosstalk may contribute to HFpEF pathology and highlights potential biomarker or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Identification of active sequences in HIV-1 molecular transmission networks using machine learning: a cross-sectional study in Hainan Province, south China.
papers.abstract: New HIV-1 infections continue to increase in Hainan Province, a major tourist destination in southern China characterized by high population mobility and diverse viral subtypes. Understanding transmission dynamics within molecular networks is critical for precision prevention.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study applies machine learning to HIV-1 molecular transmission networks in Hainan Province, China, to identify which network sequences are actively transmitting. By distinguishing active from non-active transmission clusters, the approach aims to support more precise, targeted HIV prevention in a high-mobility tourist region with diverse viral subtypes.

papers.title: Multimodal biomarkers and prediction models for stricturing and penetrating progression in Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease can progress from non-stricturing, non-penetrating inflammation (B1) to stricturing (B2) or penetrating (B3) complications, yet risk is commonly recognized only after structural damage is established. This narrative review examines clinical, endoscopic, genomic, circulating, stool, tissue, imaging, radiomic, and computational biomarkers relevant to behavioral-progression risk and separates direct B1-to-B2 or source-defined B3 evidence from related prognostic and mechanistic evidence, while distinguishing internal penetrating from perianal fistulizing disease when source reporti
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys clinical, endoscopic, genomic, circulating, stool, tissue, imaging, radiomic, and computational biomarkers that may predict progression of Crohn's disease from inflammatory (B1) to stricturing (B2) or penetrating (B3) phenotypes. It emphasizes distinguishing direct evidence of behavioral progression from related prognostic or mechanistic findings, and separates internal penetrating from perianal fistulizing disease. The review aims to frame multimodal biomarker and prediction-model development for earlier risk stratification.

papers.title: A dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework for exploratory classification of colorectal cancer histopathology and hepatocellular carcinoma clinical records.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain major diagnostic challenges because classification often depends on modality-specific evidence that is stored in separate public datasets. This study evaluates a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework using two independent and unpaired data sources: colorectal histopathological image patches and structured HCC clinical-biochemical records. The study is therefore positioned as an exploratory investigation of representation learning across heterogeneous medical datasets. The CNN branch extracts spatial and glandular texture features from
papers.summary: This study presents a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework that separately processes colorectal cancer histopathology image patches and structured hepatocellular carcinoma clinical-biochemical records, treating them as independent, unpaired data sources. The work is framed as an exploratory investigation of representation learning across heterogeneous medical datasets rather than a unified diagnostic model. It demonstrates a modular deep learning approach for modality-specific classification tasks.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning models to predict venous thromboembolism in sepsis patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Sepsis patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face a substantially elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet prediction tools tailored for this population are lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate interpretable machine learning models for predicting in-hospital VTE in septic patients with T2DM.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates interpretable machine learning models to predict in-hospital venous thromboembolism (VTE) in sepsis patients who also have type 2 diabetes mellitus, a population at elevated VTE risk for whom tailored prediction tools were previously lacking. The work addresses a specific clinical gap by combining ML prediction with interpretability, though the abstract provides limited detail on model performance and validation cohorts.

papers.title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrated multi-model AI pipelines can accelerate the discovery and design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) as alternatives to conventional antibiotics in the face of rising antimicrobial resistance. It highlights how AI can help overcome key bottlenecks such as peptide instability, potency, and cytotoxicity that hinder clinical translation. The paper outlines strategies for mining and designing novel AMPs using combined computational models.

papers.title: Association between insulin resistance-related indices and cardiovascular disease in patients with atopic dermatitis: mutual validation using real-world and NHANES data.
papers.abstract: The number of patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) who develop cardiovascular disease (CVD) has been increasing year by year. However, reliable biomarkers for identifying AD patients with a higher burden of prevalent CVD remain lacking.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether insulin resistance-related indices can serve as biomarkers for cardiovascular disease (CVD) in patients with atopic dermatitis (AD), a population with rising CVD incidence. Using both real-world clinical data and NHANES survey data for mutual validation, the authors identify associations between insulin resistance measures and prevalent CVD burden in AD patients. The findings suggest these indices may help stratify AD patients at higher cardiovascular risk.

papers.title: Multi-scale Gaussian product-of-experts for missing sequence multiple sclerosis lesion segmentation.
papers.abstract: To develop and evaluate a unified framework for multiple sclerosis (MS) white matter lesion segmentation that operates robustly under clinically prevalent missing sequence magnetic resonance imaging conditions.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a multi-scale Gaussian product-of-experts framework for segmenting multiple sclerosis lesions in MRI when some sequences are missing, a common clinical scenario. The method aims to maintain robust segmentation performance despite incomplete multi-modal input, addressing a practical limitation of existing approaches that assume all sequences are available.

papers.title: Identification of Crohn's disease-associated molecular signatures by integrative bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with rising global incidence. Its multifactorial etiology involves genetic, environmental, microbial, and immunological factors. Current diagnostic methods are invasive and costly, underscoring the need for improved biomarkers and non-invasive tools for early detection and monitoring.
papers.summary: This study integrates public gene expression datasets with bioinformatics analyses to identify molecular signatures associated with Crohn's disease, then validates key findings experimentally. The work aims to surface candidate biomarkers that could support less invasive diagnosis and monitoring of this chronic inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Emergence of OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST5994, a sister lineage of the high-risk ST307 clone.
papers.abstract: Carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (CP-KP) represents a major public health threat. The global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance is largely driven by high-risk clones (HRCs), such as ST307/OXA-48, ST11/OXA-48 and ST512/KPC-3, which currently dominate the epidemiology of CP-KP in Spain. This study aimed to describe the emergence, dissemination and genomic evolution of an OXA-48-producing K. pneumoniae ST5994 clone in Cantabria, Spain, and to characterize its genomic, phenotypic and epidemiological features.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study describes the emergence of a new OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae clone, ST5994, in Cantabria, Spain, which is a close relative (sister lineage) of the high-risk ST307 clone. The authors characterize its genomic, phenotypic, and epidemiological features to understand how it emerged and spread. The finding highlights ongoing evolution of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella and the potential for new high-risk clones to arise from existing ones.

papers.title: Early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke: an explainable model based on routine clinical data.
papers.abstract: Accurate early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke is essential for prognostic communication, early management planning, and resource allocation. However, clinically applicable and interpretable prediction tools based on routinely collected data remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops an explainable machine learning model that uses routinely collected clinical data to predict 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke. The model aims to support early prognostic communication and management planning, with interpretability features to aid clinical adoption. The abstract does not report specific performance metrics or validation results.
